format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "Working from home is better for employees than working in an office." Give reasons or examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Many companies began allowing employees to work from home in recent years, and some people now believe that this is better than working in an office. Although remote work has clear advantages, I disagree with the idea that it is always better for employees.

First, working in an office makes communication much easier. When colleagues sit near each other, they can solve small problems in a few minutes by simply talking. At home, the same problem might require several e-mails or a scheduled video call. For example, when my team worked fully remotely, a simple question about a client's order sometimes took an entire day to answer because the person who knew the answer was in other online meetings.

Second, the office helps employees separate their work and private lives. At home, many people find it difficult to stop working in the evening because their laptop is always nearby. A friend of mine who works from home told me that she often answers e-mails at ten or eleven at night. Over time, this kind of habit can lead to stress and exhaustion.

Third, young employees in particular learn a great deal by watching experienced coworkers. In an office, they can observe how senior staff handle phone calls, negotiate with clients, and run meetings. This kind of informal learning is very hard to reproduce online.

Of course, working from home saves commuting time and can be more comfortable. For this reason, I think a mixed system, in which employees spend a few days a week at home and the rest in the office, is the best solution. However, if I had to choose only one option, I would say that the office is better for most employees because it supports communication, a healthy work-life balance, and professional growth.
explanation: 序論で立場を明示し、本論で理由3つ（意思疎通・公私の区別・学び）を具体例とともに展開、譲歩の後に結論を述べる構成。 理由と具体例の充実度・構成・語彙と文法の幅で評価される。

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Some people prefer to work for one company for their entire career. Others prefer to change jobs several times. Which do you think is better? Use specific reasons and examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
In the past, many workers stayed with one company from graduation until retirement. Today, however, changing jobs has become much more common. In my opinion, changing jobs a few times during a career is better for most people, for the following reasons.

To begin with, working for different companies allows people to develop a wider range of skills. Each organization has its own systems, customers, and ways of solving problems. For instance, my older brother worked first for a small software company, where he had to handle many different tasks, and then moved to a large bank, where he learned how big projects are managed. Because of these two experiences, he is now a project leader who understands both flexible and structured approaches.

In addition, changing jobs can lead to better pay and more responsibility. When employees stay in one place, their salary often increases slowly. By contrast, a person with valuable experience can negotiate a higher salary or a better title at a new company. This also motivates workers to keep improving their abilities.

Furthermore, changing jobs helps people find work that truly suits them. Many young people choose their first job without knowing exactly what they enjoy. After a few years, they may discover that they prefer a different field. Moving to a new company gives them a chance to follow their real interests, which usually makes them happier and more productive.

Admittedly, staying with one company has benefits, such as job security and deep knowledge of the organization. Changing jobs too often may also make an employer doubt a person's commitment. Nevertheless, I believe that changing jobs two or three times, after gaining solid experience at each company, is the best way to grow professionally and find a satisfying career.
explanation: To begin with / In addition / Furthermore で理由を整理し、Admittedly で反対意見に触れてから結論に戻ると論理的。 理由と具体例の充実度・構成・語彙と文法の幅で評価される。

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "Smartphones have made people's lives better." Give reasons or examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Smartphones have become a part of almost everyone's daily life. Some people say that they cause problems, but I agree that smartphones have made people's lives better overall.

The first reason is that smartphones make communication easy and fast. In the past, people needed a computer or a home telephone to contact others. Now, we can send messages, make video calls, and share photos anywhere and at any time. For example, my parents live in another city, but I can see their faces and talk with them every weekend through video calls. This helps us feel close even though we live far apart.

The second reason is that smartphones help people save time. With a smartphone, I can check train times, pay bills, buy tickets, and find directions in just a few seconds. Last month, when my train was canceled, I quickly found another route on a map app and arrived at my meeting on time. Without my smartphone, I would have been very late.

The third reason is that smartphones give people access to information and learning. Many people use apps to study languages, read the news, or watch lessons on various topics. I study English for fifteen minutes on the train every morning with an app, and my vocabulary has improved a lot.

Of course, smartphones also have some disadvantages. Some people spend too much time on social media, and this can affect their sleep or their work. However, this is a problem of how people use smartphones, not of the smartphones themselves. If we use them wisely, the benefits are much greater than the problems.

For these reasons, I believe smartphones have made our lives more convenient, connected, and productive.

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Some companies offer training through online courses, while others prefer in-person workshops. Which method do you think is more effective for employees? Give specific reasons and examples. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Training is essential for employees who want to improve their skills and for companies that want to stay competitive. Nowadays, many companies use online courses instead of traditional workshops. While online training is convenient, I believe that in-person workshops are more effective for most employees.

The main reason is that in-person workshops allow participants to interact directly with the instructor and with each other. When employees have questions, they can ask them immediately and receive detailed answers. They can also learn from their colleagues' questions and experiences. For example, at a customer service workshop I attended last year, we practiced handling complaints in small groups. The instructor watched each group and gave us specific advice, which I still use in my job today. It would be difficult to have the same experience by watching a video.

Another reason is that workshops help employees concentrate. When people take an online course at their desks, they are often interrupted by e-mails, phone calls, or coworkers. Many of my colleagues admit that they play online training videos in the background while doing other work. In a workshop, by contrast, participants are away from their daily tasks and can focus completely on learning.

Finally, in-person workshops build relationships between employees from different departments. During breaks and group activities, people get to know each other, and these connections can make future teamwork smoother.

It is true that online courses are cheaper and more flexible, and they are useful for simple topics such as learning a new software function. However, for skills that require practice and discussion, such as leadership, negotiation, or customer service, in-person workshops produce much better results. Therefore, I think companies should continue to invest in face-to-face training.
explanation: 比較型の問題では一方を選び、もう一方の利点も認めつつ「どんな場合に」優れているかを限定すると説得力が出る。 理由と具体例の充実度・構成・語彙と文法の幅で評価される。

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: What do you think is the most important characteristic of a good manager? Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
A manager has a strong influence on how employees feel about their work. There are many important qualities for a good manager, such as knowledge, decision-making skills, and fairness. In my opinion, however, the most important characteristic is the ability to listen to employees.

First, a manager who listens can understand problems before they become serious. Employees often notice problems with customers, products, or work processes earlier than their managers. If the manager listens carefully, these problems can be solved quickly. For example, at my previous job, a coworker told our manager that customers were confused by our new order form. The manager listened, changed the form within a week, and the number of customer complaints went down.

Second, listening makes employees feel respected. When a manager asks for their opinions and takes them seriously, employees feel that they are an important part of the team. As a result, they become more motivated and are more likely to share new ideas. In contrast, when a manager never listens, employees stop speaking up, and the team loses many good ideas.

Third, a manager who listens can support employees better. Every worker has different strengths and challenges. By having regular conversations with each team member, a manager can learn who needs more training, who wants more responsibility, and who is having difficulty. Then the manager can give the right kind of help to each person.

Of course, a manager also needs knowledge and leadership skills. However, without the ability to listen, these skills cannot be used effectively. For these reasons, I believe that listening is the most important characteristic of a good manager.
explanation: 「最も重要な特徴」を1つに絞り、理由3つと具体例で論じる。冒頭で他の候補にも触れると視野の広さを示せる。 理由と具体例の充実度・構成・語彙と文法の幅で評価される。

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "Companies should spend money on protecting the environment even if it reduces their profits." Give reasons or examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Today, environmental problems such as climate change and pollution are serious concerns around the world. Some people argue that a company's main goal is to make a profit, but I agree that companies should spend money to protect the environment, even if their profits decrease in the short term.

First, companies have a responsibility to society. Businesses use natural resources, energy, and water, and many of them produce waste. Since their activities affect the environment, they should also help reduce the damage. For example, a factory that releases chemicals into a river harms the people and wildlife that depend on that river. Investing in cleaner technology is a fair way for the company to take responsibility for its impact.

Second, environmental efforts can actually benefit companies in the long run. More and more customers prefer to buy products from companies that act responsibly. A clothing company that uses recycled materials, for instance, can attract young customers who care about the environment. In addition, saving energy by installing solar panels or efficient lighting may be expensive at first, but it reduces electricity costs over time.

Third, protecting the environment helps companies attract and keep good employees. Many workers, especially younger ones, want to work for organizations that share their values. A friend of mine chose her current employer partly because the company had a strong recycling program and encouraged employees to commute by bicycle.

Some people worry that spending on the environment will make a company less competitive. However, governments are introducing stricter environmental laws, so companies that act early will be better prepared in the future. For all of these reasons, I strongly believe that companies should invest in protecting the environment, even if it reduces their profits for a while.

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Some people prefer to spend their vacations at home, while others prefer to travel. Which do you prefer? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Vacations are important because they give people a chance to rest and enjoy themselves. Some people like to stay at home during their holidays, but I prefer to travel, for several reasons.

First, traveling allows me to have new experiences. When I visit a different city or country, I can see famous places, try local food, and learn about other cultures. For example, last year I traveled to a small town by the sea. I tried fresh seafood that I had never eaten before and learned how the local people catch fish. These experiences gave me memories that I still talk about with my friends.

Second, traveling helps me relax more completely. When I stay at home, I often think about my work, check my e-mail, or do housework such as cleaning and laundry. As a result, I don't feel that I am really on vacation. When I travel, however, I am far away from my daily routine, so I can forget about my responsibilities for a while and truly rest.

Third, traveling is a good way to spend time with family and friends. During a trip, we spend the whole day together, and we often face small challenges, such as finding a restaurant or reading a map in another language. Solving these problems together makes our relationships stronger.

Of course, traveling can be expensive and tiring, and staying at home is cheaper and more comfortable. However, I think the new experiences and memories that travel brings are worth the cost. For these reasons, I prefer to spend my vacations traveling rather than staying at home.

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Many employees say that their companies hold too many meetings. Do you agree that meetings are often a waste of time? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Meetings are a common part of office life, and many employees complain that they spend too much time in them. I agree that meetings are often a waste of time, although I also believe that well-planned meetings can be very valuable.

The main reason many meetings waste time is that they lack a clear purpose. Some teams hold a meeting every week simply because it is on the calendar, even when there is nothing important to discuss. At my company, for example, our weekly department meeting often consists of people reading updates that could easily be shared by e-mail. Twenty people sitting in a room for an hour means twenty hours of work time lost.

Another problem is that too many people are invited. Managers often invite everyone who might be slightly interested in a topic. As a result, many participants have nothing to contribute, and they sit quietly while thinking about the work they cannot do. In addition, when there are many people, discussions take longer and decisions are harder to make.

Finally, many meetings run longer than planned because no one controls the discussion. Without a clear agenda and a time limit, people may change the subject or repeat the same points.

However, this does not mean that meetings are useless. When a meeting has a clear goal, an agenda, and only the necessary participants, it can solve problems much faster than a long chain of e-mails. Brainstorming sessions and discussions about difficult decisions are good examples.

In conclusion, I agree that many meetings waste time, mainly because of poor planning. Companies should hold fewer but better-organized meetings, so that employees can use their time more effectively.
explanation: 賛成の理由を3つ挙げたうえで「良い会議の条件」を示すと、単純な賛否を超えた深い議論になる。 理由と具体例の充実度・構成・語彙と文法の幅で評価される。

Meetings are a common part of office life, and many employees complain that they spend too much time in them. I agree that meetings are often a waste of time, although I also believe that well-planned meetings can be very valuable.

The main reason many meetings waste time is that they lack a clear purpose. Some teams hold a meeting every week simply because it is on the calendar, even when there is nothing important to discuss. At my company, for example, our weekly department meeting often consists of people reading updates that could easily be shared by e-mail. Twenty people sitting in a room for an hour means twenty hours of work time lost.

Another problem is that too many people are invited. Managers often invite everyone who might be slightly interested in a topic. As a result, many participants have nothing to contribute, and they sit quietly while thinking about the work they cannot do. In addition, when there are many people, discussions take longer and decisions are harder to make.

Finally, many meetings run longer than planned because no one controls the discussion. Without a clear agenda and a time limit, people may change the subject or repeat the same points.

However, this does not mean that meetings are useless. When a meeting has a clear goal, an agenda, and only the necessary participants, it can solve problems much faster than a long chain of e-mails. Brainstorming sessions and discussions about difficult decisions are good examples.

In conclusion, I agree that many meetings waste time, mainly because of poor planning. Companies should hold fewer but better-organized meetings, so that employees can use their time more effectively.

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Some people think it is better to live in a big city. Others think it is better to live in a small town. Which do you prefer and why? (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Where we live has a big effect on our daily lives. Some people enjoy the excitement of a big city, while others prefer the quiet life of a small town. Personally, I would rather live in a small town, for the following reasons.

First, life in a small town is less stressful. Big cities are crowded and noisy, and people often have to spend a long time on packed trains or in traffic jams. In a small town, there is less traffic, and most places can be reached in a short time. For example, my uncle lives in a small town, and he can walk to his office in ten minutes. He says that he has much more free time than when he lived in the city.

Second, the cost of living is usually lower in a small town. Rent, in particular, is much cheaper. With the same salary, people can live in a larger home and save more money. This is especially important for families with children.

Third, people in small towns often have closer relationships with their neighbors. Because the community is small, people know each other and help each other when there is a problem. When my uncle was sick last winter, his neighbors brought him food and cleared the snow in front of his house.

It is true that big cities have more job opportunities, shopping centers, and entertainment. However, thanks to the Internet, many people can now work remotely and shop online, even if they live in a small town. For these reasons, I believe that living in a small town offers a more comfortable and balanced life.

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "In the future, computers and machines will do most of the work that people do today." Give reasons or examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Advances in technology have already changed the way people work, and some experts predict that machines will eventually replace most human workers. While I agree that technology will take over many tasks, I disagree with the claim that computers and machines will do most of the work people do today.

It is certainly true that machines are becoming more capable. Factories use robots to assemble products, and software can now answer simple customer questions, translate documents, and analyze large amounts of data. Tasks that are repetitive and follow clear rules are especially likely to be automated. For example, many supermarkets have introduced self-checkout machines, which has reduced the number of cashiers needed.

However, a large portion of work requires abilities that machines still lack. Jobs in healthcare, education, and social services depend heavily on empathy and personal relationships. A patient who has just received bad news needs a doctor or nurse who can understand their feelings and respond with kindness. Similarly, teachers do much more than deliver information; they motivate students and notice when a child is struggling.

Moreover, history shows that new technology tends to change jobs rather than eliminate work altogether. When computers became common in offices, some clerical positions disappeared, but entirely new professions, such as Web designers and data analysts, were created. I expect the same pattern to continue. As machines handle routine tasks, people will spend more time on creative work, problem solving, and supervising the machines themselves.

In conclusion, computers and machines will undoubtedly take over many specific tasks, and some jobs will disappear. Nevertheless, because human skills such as empathy and creativity remain essential, and because technology tends to create new types of work, I believe that people will continue to do most of the work in the future, even if that work looks very different from today's.

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? "Companies should organize social events, such as parties or sports days, for their employees." Give reasons or examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
Many companies organize social events such as year-end parties, picnics, or sports days. Some people think these events are unnecessary, but I agree that companies should organize them for their employees.

First, social events help employees build good relationships. At work, people usually talk only about their tasks, and they rarely communicate with people from other departments. At a party or sports day, however, they can have casual conversations and learn about each other's hobbies and families. For example, at my company's summer barbecue last year, I talked with a coworker from the sales department for the first time. Since then, it has been much easier for me to ask him questions about our customers.

Second, social events can improve teamwork. When employees play games or sports together, they need to cooperate and communicate to win. These experiences make it easier for them to work together on real projects later. Members of a team who know and trust each other usually solve problems more quickly.

Third, social events show that the company cares about its employees. When a company spends time and money to create an enjoyable event, employees feel appreciated. This can increase their motivation and make them more likely to stay with the company for a long time.

However, companies should be careful not to force employees to attend events, especially on weekends or late at night. Events should be held during working hours or at convenient times, and attendance should be optional. If companies follow these points, social events can be enjoyable for everyone.

For these reasons, I believe social events are a good investment for companies.

format: Writing Q8 意見を記述する
question: When hiring new employees, some companies focus on applicants' work experience, while others focus on their education. Which do you think is more important? Give reasons or examples to support your opinion. (Writing time: 30 minutes. Aim for about 300 words.)
answer:
When companies hire new staff, they usually look at two main things: what the applicants have studied and what they have done in previous jobs. Both are valuable, but in my opinion, work experience is more important in most cases.

First, work experience shows that a person can actually apply knowledge in real situations. A university degree proves that someone has learned theories, but it does not guarantee that the person can use them under pressure, with real customers and real deadlines. For example, an applicant who has managed a store for three years has already dealt with staff shortages, unhappy customers, and sales targets. Such a person can usually contribute to a new company much faster than a graduate with no practical experience.

Second, experience demonstrates important personal qualities. Employers want workers who are reliable, who communicate well, and who can work in a team. These qualities are difficult to measure through grades, but a strong work history and good references from former employers show them clearly.

Third, hiring experienced workers reduces training costs. New graduates often need months of training before they can work independently. Experienced employees, on the other hand, already understand basic business practices, so the company can spend less time and money preparing them.

That said, education is still essential in certain fields. Doctors, engineers, and lawyers, for instance, must have specialized degrees before they can work at all. Moreover, for entry-level positions, companies have no choice but to look at education, since applicants have little experience.

Overall, however, for most positions, I believe that work experience is a better indicator of how well a person will perform. Therefore, companies should give it more weight when making hiring decisions.
explanation: That said で例外（専門職・新卒採用）を認め、Overall で主張に戻る構成。主張の範囲を適切に限定している点が評価される。 理由と具体例の充実度・構成・語彙と文法の幅で評価される。
